info.title: ResellingKori Partner API
info.summary: Sell ResellingKori products from your own website or app, at your own prices.
info.description:
You sell to your customer at **your** price. ResellingKori packs and ships the parcel, the courier collects the
cash you tell it to collect, and you keep the difference between your selling price and the ResellingKori price.

This is the same API the ResellingKori WooCommerce Connector plugin uses. Everything a WooCommerce reseller can
do, your site can do too.

**Revision 3.1** · signing **RK2** · order schema **2** · currency **BDT** (the only currency).

## Authentication (every request)

Four headers, no cookies, no bearer token. The secret is never sent.

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `X-RK-Key` | your Key ID (`rkk_…`) |
| `X-RK-Timestamp` | current Unix time in seconds (the server accepts ±300 s) |
| `X-RK-Nonce` | 16–64 characters `A–Z a–z 0–9 _ -`, new for every request (use 32 random hex characters) |
| `X-RK-Signature` | lower-case hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical string below, keyed with your secret (`rks_…`) |

```
canonical = "RK2" LF timestamp LF nonce LF METHOD LF route LF query LF sha256_hex(body)
```

* `route` – the path **without** `/wp-json` and without `?…`, for example `/rk/v1/orders` or `/rk/v1/products/5120`.
* `query` – all query parameters sorted by name, names and values RFC 3986-encoded (space is `%20`, never `+`),
  joined as `a=1&b=2`; the empty string when there is none.
* `body` – the exact bytes you send (empty for GET). Serialise once, hash, send the same bytes.
* No trailing line feed.

Test vectors (secret `rks_test_secret`, timestamp `1700000000`, nonce `0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef`):

| Request | Signature |
|---|---|
| `GET /rk/v1/products/search?q=awei y526&per_page=20` | `c69632110d86a75fc480e6fd8b319ae3d96336600cfc5a3498dcd90e0eb49620` |
| `POST /rk/v1/orders` with body `{"external_order_id":"1058"}` | `efa3d6bdd0c94c34ba44106831ebc83b17a4d84ec0ef34c74b27cf46e1482779` |

The ready clients in this kit (PHP, Node.js, Python, Postman) do all of this for you.

## Permissions

Each key carries a list of permissions: `catalog:read`, `orders:read`, `orders:write`, `webhooks:manage`.
A request without the permission it needs is answered `403 rkapi_scope_denied` (`data.required`, `data.granted`).
`GET /ping` and the reading half of `POST /connection` need none.

## Money

Amounts are strings in BDT with two decimals (`"1190.00"`); arithmetic on the server is exact (integer paisa).

## Errors

Every error is `{ "code": "rkapi_…", "message": "…", "data": { "status": 422, … } }`. Branch on `code`.
Retry the **same** request (same body, same `external_order_id`, a new nonce) only after network errors, `5xx`,
`408`, `425`, `429`, `rkapi_in_progress` and `rkapi_busy`. Every other `4xx` is final.

## Idempotency

`POST /orders` is idempotent on `external_order_id`. After a timeout or a `5xx`, call `GET /orders/lookup` first;
if the order is not found, send the identical body again. The official clients do exactly this in `createOrder`.

servers.description: ResellingKori production (the route you sign is the path after /wp-json, for example /rk/v1/orders)

tags.name: Connection
tags.description: Check your credentials, permissions and limits; register your webhook.

tags.name: Orders
tags.description: Check, place, follow and cancel orders.

get.description:
Returns your store, key, sales agent, permissions and limits. Call it first: `200` with `"ok": true` means your
signing is right. `401 rkapi_auth_invalid` means the signature does not match (check the route without
`/wp-json`, the query encoding and that the body you hash is the body you send).

post.summary: Register or remove your webhook address
post.description:
Same answer as `/ping`, plus `agent_match` and `callback_result`. Registering needs the `webhooks:manage`
permission. ResellingKori sends a signed `callback.verify` event to the address and expects
`{"proof": HMAC_SHA256_hex(secret, "RK2-CALLBACK\n" + challenge)}` with HTTP 200.
At most 12 registrations per store per hour. `remove_callback: true` switches webhooks off (poll `GET /orders` instead).

200.description: Your connection and the result of the webhook change.

get.summary: The whole catalogue (paged), for import and incremental sync

parameters.name: updated_after
parameters.description: Unix seconds, or ISO 8601 (`2026-11-01T00:00:00Z`; without an offset the time is UTC). Only products changed at or after this time.

parameters.name: in_stock
parameters.description: `1` = only products in stock or on back-order.

parameters.name: hide_empty
parameters.description: `1` leaves out categories without published products.

get.description:
Words shorter than 2 characters are dropped; at most 8 words are used. A product matches if its title contains any
of the words (`SH-309` also matches `SH309`); words that contain a digit are also matched against product and
variation SKUs. Ranked by the number of matching words, then by title. No usable word: `400 rkapi_query_short`.
Up to 50 comma-separated SKUs, exact match, case-insensitive; products and variations. When a SKU belongs to a variation, `matched_variation_id` names it.

200.description: Matches by SKU and the SKUs that were not found.

get.description: A variation id resolves to its parent product (and sets `matched_variation_id`). Unpublished or missing: `404 rkapi_product_not_found`.

post.summary: Check an order without placing it (dry run)
post.description:
Same body and the same checks as `POST /orders` (catalogue, variation, price floor, price guard, stock, amounts,
limits, your sales agent), but **nothing is created or reserved**. Errors are the same as for `POST /orders`.
Stock can still run out between validate and create: only `POST /orders` reserves it.

200.description: The order would be accepted now.

post.summary: Place an order at your selling price (exactly once)
post.description:
Idempotent on `external_order_id`. `201` = created and stock reserved. `200` with `duplicate: true` = you already
sent exactly this order; the original is returned. `409 rkapi_order_conflict` = this reference was used with
different content. After a timeout or `5xx` do **not** invent a new reference: look the order up
(`GET /orders/lookup`), and if it answers `404 rkapi_order_not_found` send the identical body again.
There is no amendment: cancel and send a new order under a new reference.

200.description: Already created with exactly this content (`duplicate: true`).

get.description:
Newest change first, or oldest change first when `updated_after` is given (`order=asc|desc` overrides).
Poll every 5–15 minutes with `updated_after` = the `server_time` of your previous poll.
`gone` lists external ids of orders that were deleted on ResellingKori's side.

parameters.name: updated_after
parameters.description: Unix seconds or ISO 8601 (UTC without an offset). Compared with the order's last change.

get.summary: Find your order by your own reference
get.description:
`{ "order": Order, "state": "created | cancelled" }`; `{ "order": null, "state": "creating" }` while a creation is in
flight (wait a few seconds and look again); `404 rkapi_order_not_found` if there is none, which means sending the same
request again is safe.

200.description: The order, or the in-flight marker.

get.summary: Status of several orders by ResellingKori id

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated ResellingKori order ids (`Order.id`), at most 100.

200.description: The orders and the ids that do not belong to your store.

get.description: Orders of other stores are indistinguishable from missing ones (`404 rkapi_order_not_found`).

post.summary: Cancel an order that has not been processed yet
post.description:
Possible while `order.cancellable` is true (not yet processed, no tracking number). Cancelling twice is harmless
(`already_cancelled: true`). Otherwise `409 rkapi_not_cancellable`. Stock returns to ResellingKori.

post.summary: Order changed (sent by ResellingKori to the address you registered)
post.description:
Signed like an API request, but with the **literal route `/rkc/v1/webhook`** (whatever your real path is), an empty
query, and the extra header `X-RK-Event-Id`. Verify the signature and the ±300 s timestamp, remember nonces and event
ids for at least 10 minutes and ignore repeats, ignore an event whose `sequence` is lower than the one you already
applied for that order, answer `2xx` within 10 seconds. Network errors, `5xx`, `408`, `425` and `429` are retried
after 1, 3, 9, 27 and 81 minutes; other `4xx` are not.

The first event is `callback.verify`: answer `200 {"proof": HMAC_SHA256_hex(secret, "RK2-CALLBACK\n" + challenge)}`.
Webhooks never contain customer details.

200.description: Received. For `callback.verify` the body must be `{"proof": "…"}`.

rkTimestamp.name: X-RK-Timestamp
rkTimestamp.description: Current Unix time in seconds (±300 s).

rkNonce.name: X-RK-Nonce
rkNonce.description: New random value for every request (32 hex characters).

rkSignature.name: X-RK-Signature
rkSignature.description: Lower-case hex HMAC-SHA256 of the RK2 canonical string, keyed with your secret. See the API description.

IncludeDetails.name: include
IncludeDetails.description: `details` adds categories, images, weight, dimensions, short description and modification date; `details,description` also the HTML description. (`GET /products` always includes the details.)

Error.description:
An error. Branch on `code`. Common codes: `rkapi_auth_missing`/`rkapi_auth_invalid` (401), `rkapi_auth_expired` (401, `data.server_time`),
`rkapi_auth_replay` (401), `rkapi_key_revoked` (401), `rkapi_store_disabled` (403), `rkapi_scope_denied` (403), `rkapi_ip_denied` (403),
`rkapi_locked`/`rkapi_rate_limited` (429, `Retry-After`), `rkapi_validation`/`rkapi_amount_invalid`/`rkapi_items_invalid` (422),
`rkapi_price_changed`/`rkapi_out_of_stock`/`rkapi_order_conflict`/`rkapi_in_progress`/`rkapi_not_cancellable` (409),
`rkapi_order_not_found`/`rkapi_product_not_found` (404), `rkapi_busy` (503), `rkapi_create_failed` (500).

Money.description: Amount in BDT with two decimals.

ExternalOrderId.description: Your own order reference. Unique per order, forever.

server_time.description: On `rkapi_auth_expired`: use it to correct your clock.

ip.description: On `rkapi_ip_denied`: the address the request came from.

email_hint.description: Masked; the full address is never returned.

callback_url.description: Your https webhook address (any path, no query, public host).

expected_agent_email.description: Comparison only; it never selects an agent.

base_price.description: What you pay ResellingKori per unit.

price.description: ResellingKori's current shop price (reference only; you choose your own price).

base_price.description: **What you pay ResellingKori per unit.** Your selling price must not be lower. Empty when the product has no price.

date_modified.description: ISO 8601, UTC. Use it for incremental sync.

matches.description: SKU → product (an empty list when nothing matched).

phone.description: 10–15 digits after removing everything except digits and `+`.

external_item_id.description: Unique within the order (your line number is fine).

expected_base_unit_price.description: Optional guard: the `base_price` you showed your customer. Never used as the price; if ResellingKori's price changed the order is refused with `409 rkapi_price_changed`.

Payment.description:
`cod_amount = order_total − prepaid_amount`, where `order_total = Σ selling_unit_price × quantity + delivery_charge`.
Method `prepaid`: `prepaid_amount = order_total` and `cod_amount = 0`. You always send all three amounts.

partial.description: `true` if the parcel contains only part of your customer's order (information only).

OrderRequest.description: Fields you might be tempted to send are ignored on purpose: store, agent, key, ResellingKori price, tax, discount, order status.

raw_status.description: ResellingKori's own status (informational; do not branch on it).

sequence.description: Grows with every change you can observe; never apply an older sequence over a newer one.

error.description: Set when ResellingKori needs your attention (for example the courier could not reach the customer).

existing_order.description: Tells you when the reference was already used.

type.description: Unknown types mean "the order changed": use `data.order` as the truth.
